profile.stagger_pattern: Four ward seats (A, B, C, D) plus one at-large seat. Charter s.3.2(a): Wards C and D are elected together (2018, 2022, and every four years thereafter); Wards A and B plus the At-Large seat are elected together (2020, 2024, and every four years thereafter). Elections were held in MAY through 2020 with terms beginning July 1; Virginia's SB 1157 (2021) moved them to NOVEMBER effective for elections after 2022-01-01, and Va. Code s.24.2-222.1 bars shortening terms, so sitting terms were EXTENDED rather than cut: the Ward C/D terms elected May 2018 ran to 2022-12-31 instead of 2022-06-30, and the Ward A/B/At-Large terms elected May 2020 ran to 2024-12-31 instead of 2024-06-30. From the November cycles onward, members take office January 1 following election. There was consequently NO Waynesboro council contest in November 2018 or November 2020 - a structural fact, not a gap.

run_log.detail: Read agent-brief.md and the state-registry Virginia + cross-state sections. Registry flagged Waynesboro's mayor-selection method as UNVERIFIED; that was the primary question to settle.

Census finding CONFIRMED: the www host is robots-blocked but the bare host waynesboro.va.us serves everything to plain curl with a browser UA. The CivicPlus AgendaCenter DATED SEARCH endpoint /AgendaCenter/Search/?term=&CIDs=1&startDate=&endDate= returned a complete per-year minutes index for 2018-2026 at zero search cost - {KIND} is 'Minutes' (not 'ArchivedMinutes') and no integer sweep was needed. The index alone revealed the cycle calendar: organizational meetings sit in EARLY JULY through 2022 and in EARLY JANUARY from 2023 onward, which is the structural tell for the May->November election move. Note: the term= parameter searches document TITLES only, not full text, so it is useless as a mid-term-change probe.

MAYOR-SELECTION QUESTION SETTLED FROM THE CHARTER. https://law.lis.virginia.gov/charters/waynesboro/ s.3.2(a): council is five members - one resident each of Wards A, B, C, D plus one at large; s.3.4(c): 'The council shall elect one of its members as mayor' and likewise a vice mayor; s.3.4(d): two-year mayoral term. Charter also fixes the stagger (Wards C+D in 2022 and every four years; Wards A+B+At-Large in 2024 and every four years) and that members take office January 1 following election. The registry's 'Waynesboro unverified' entry is now resolved: COUNCIL-SELECTED. Independently corroborated three ways: (a) the 2022 state portal locality page lists Ward C and Ward D council contests and NO mayoral contest; (b) the 2024 canvass sweep found council contests only; (c) every organizational meeting's minutes record a motion and roll-call vote 'to appoint ... as Mayor for the two-year term ending ...'.

Pulled the ten organizational-meeting minutes PDFs (2018-07-02, 2019-07-08, 2020-07-13, 2021-07-12, 2022-07-11, 2023-01-03, 2024-01-08, 2025-01-13, 2026-01-12) plus the 2019-01-14 business meeting via /AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_MMDDYYYY-NNN and extracted them locally with pdftotext -layout. These give verbatim PRESENT/ABSENT rosters and verbatim mayor/vice-mayor appointment votes for every year of the panel. WebFetch was never needed for these; plain curl + local extraction kept the summarizer out of the trust path entirely.

2022-11-08 sourced from the one surviving state-portal folder, exactly as the registry describes: .../2022%20November%20General/Site/Locality/WAYNESBORO_CITY/Index.html returned Member City Council (WARD C) Kenny Lee 752 def. Jeremy D. Sloat 699, and (WARD D) Jim Wood 1,128 def. Samuel A. Hostetter 1,111. Confirmed by direct fetch that four other year-folders (2024 November General, 2020 May General, and two name variants) 404 in both Site/ and Json/ forms - the registry's 'orphaned snapshot' finding still holds as of 2026-08-17.

2024-11-05 sourced via the historical.elections.virginia.gov NUMERIC route (coordinator tip - the registry's 'deep links all 404' entry is WRONG for the numeric form). Seeded from id 161542, swept the CSV API https://va2.elstats.civera.com/api/download_contest/{id}_table.csv concurrently; localities are alphabetical within an election, so Waynesboro sits between Virginia Beach and Winchester. Found: 161700 City Council At-Large (Jeremy D. Sloat 5,064 def. Robert W. 'Bobby' Henderson 4,605, write-ins 123, total 9,792); 161702 City Council Ward A (Lorie Jean Strother 994 def. David W. 'Major Dave' Goetze 765); 161704 City Council Ward B (Terry R. Short Jr. 1,704 def. William H. Flory 1,264). Precinct-level breakdowns included. NOTE for the registry: my client (urllib) follows redirects by default, so the missing -L trap did not apply here.

The MAY 2020 cycle is NOT in the historical.elections.virginia.gov contest API. Verified by exhaustion: the Nov 2020 band is 144560-144821 (Waynesboro absent from it, which independently confirms there was no November 2020 council contest), the 2018 band is ~134000-135900 (Waynesboro also absent, confirming its May calendar), and every id sampled between 140000 and 144555 returns HTTP 500. Sourced the cycle at Rung 4 instead. VPAP was tried on four dates (20200505, 20200519, 20221108, 20241105) and is DEAD: HTTP 202 with zero bytes to curl on all four, HTTP 403 to WebFetch. Ballotpedia's Waynesboro city-elections page 404s to curl.

2020-05-19 cycle sourced from the News Virginian headline 'Terry Short, Bruce Allen keep council seats; Lana Williams wins Ward A' (the body is paywalled/ROT13-obfuscated but the headline, deck and photo caption extract cleanly: 'Short won re-election for his second term with 57% of overall votes'). Three seats - Ward A, Ward B, At-Large - matching the charter stagger. The 2024 News Virginian piece extracts a clean lede confirming ward assignment: 'Waynesboro City Councilman Terry Short won reelection to his Ward B seat Tuesday. He will be joined on Council by newcomers Republican at-large candidate Jeremy Sloat and independent Ward A candidate Lorie Strother.' CAVEAT: the 2020-05-19 date reflects the statewide COVID postponement of the May 5 general; the city's own 2020-05-01 'City Council and Board of Elections Emergency Joint Meeting' notice is consistent with it, but I did not find a Waynesboro-specific verbatim naming the date. The seating itself is independently sourced at high confidence from the 2020-07-13 organizational minutes, so no tenure depends on the date.

ONE mid-term change in the window, fully dated from primary source. Elzena Anderson (Ward A) is present in the 2020-02-24 minutes and gone from the 2020-03-09 roster (four members listed). Verbatim from the 2020-03-09 minutes: 'APPOINTMENT OF INTERIM WARD A COUNCIL PERSON: Vice Mayor Henderson moved to appoint Ms. Jeanie McCutcheon as the Interim Ward A Council person, completing the term of Ms. Elzena Anderson, for an unexpired four-year term ending June 30, 2020,' adopted 4:0, with a Clerk's Note that McCutcheon took her Oath of Office administered by the City Manager that same evening. The 2020-03-05 minutes record 'INTERVIEW OF INTERIM WARD A COUNCIL MEMBER CANDIDATES'. A WebSearch corroborates Anderson's resignation as effective 2020-03-01. Continuity then verified across the whole panel by spot-checking PRESENT blocks in 2020-06, 2021-06, 2021-12, 2023-06, 2024-06 and 2025-06 minutes: no other change of composition. 2020-03-09 was a Monday and 2023-01-03 a Tuesday, both matching the minutes' own day-of-week statements.

SEAT LABELS resolved from agenda cover-page headers, which print each member's ward - a reusable CivicPlus technique found via the site search /Search/Results?searchPhrase=. 2020-05-01 notice (documentcenter/view/9325): SHORT Mayor AT LARGE / HENDERSON Vice Mayor WARD C / ALLEN WARD B / HOSTETTER WARD D / McCUTCHEON WARD A. 2021 agenda (documentcenter/view/9942): HENDERSON Mayor WARD C / WILLIAMS Vice Mayor WARD A / ALLEN WARD B / SHORT AT LARGE. 2026 agendas: LEE Mayor WARD C / AKANBI Vice Mayor WARD A / SHORT WARD B / WOOD WARD D / SLOAT AT LARGE. This exposes a SEAT SWITCH that a naive reading would miss: Terry Short held the AT-LARGE seat 2019-2024 and then won the WARD B seat in Nov 2024 - two distinct tenure rows, not one continuous one. Also note Bobby Henderson, defeated for Ward C in 2022, ran again for the At-Large seat in 2024 and lost to Sloat - a winner/loser pair that would invite a false continuity inference.

TERM-EXTENSION mechanics confirmed verbatim rather than assumed. The 2022-07-11 organizational minutes record council moving the terms of its charter officers, liaison officers, Finance Committee members, Acting Clerk, 'the mayor and the vice mayor to terminate on January 1, 2023' - i.e. Henderson's mayoralty and Williams's vice-mayoralty, both nominally expiring 2022-06-30, were extended to bridge to the new January organizational calendar. Both were still seated as Mayor and Vice Mayor at the 2023-01-03 meeting, where Williams was elevated to mayor. Name change captured: Lorie Jean Strother (ballot name, Nov 2024) = Lorie Jean Akanbi (seated name, from Jan 2025) - recorded in name_variants; merging or splitting these would have broken the Ward A chain.

ACFR route not needed and not pursued to completion - the minutes spine already covers every seat-year at high confidence. For the record, the city's CivicPlus site search surfaces an Annual Comprehensive Financial Report presentation in the 2021-12-13 minutes, so a series does appear to exist if a future pass needs an independent officials spine. The Virginia Auditor of Public Accounts off-domain mirror was not reached within the cap.

56 of 56 seat-years sourced (7 stable seat labels - Ward A, Ward B, Ward C, Ward D, At-Large, Mayor, Vice Mayor - across 2019-2026). Zero gaps, zero low-confidence rows, zero unrecovered cycles. File written after the cycle calendar and rewritten at completion.
